observations: Two photos show the same electronic keyboard wrapped in clear plastic, standing upright against a door frame.
Full-size keyboard, approx 61 black and white keys, silver/grey body.
Control panel includes a rotary dial, numeric buttons, a small LCD display, and various function buttons.
No power adapter, stand, bag, or box visible in either photo.
No readable brand or model text visible on the casing in either photo; a dark panel near the display could hold a logo but it is not legible.
Background shows an outdoor/indoor threshold with tiled floor, a person's bare feet and a patterned skirt visible to the right.
Watermark 'MARY OLUGBAMI POSTED ON...' overlays both images, indicating a reposted/stock listing photo rather than a fresh seller photo.

claims.evidence: No shipping label, import tag, or UK marking visible in either photo; origin cannot be confirmed from images.
No audio/video provided; sound output cannot be judged from still photos.

risks.risk: Keyboard may not power on or may have non-working keys/buttons since it is untested in photos.
risks.proof: A short video of the seller powering it on and pressing several keys across the full range, with audible sound.
risks.if_unproven: priced as not working / non-functional unit

risks.risk: No power adapter included, which is required to operate the keyboard.
risks.proof: A photo of the actual power adapter/cord being sold with the unit.
risks.if_unproven: priced as unit only, without adapter

risks.risk: Brand and model are unidentified, so true market value tier (budget vs mid-range) cannot be set.
risks.proof: A clear close-up photo of the brand logo and model number, usually near the display or on the back.
risks.if_unproven: priced at the lowest plausible tier for a generic unbranded 61-key keyboard

risks.risk: Physical condition under the plastic wrap (scratches, cracked keys, missing buttons) cannot be verified.
risks.proof: Photos with the plastic wrap removed, showing full front and back panels in good light.
risks.if_unproven: priced assuming visible wear consistent with 'used' condition, worst case cosmetic damage

proof_requests: Video of the keyboard powering on and producing sound across multiple keys and voices/demo mode.
Close-up photo of the brand/model label or sticker, typically near the display or on the rear panel.
Photo of the power adapter/cable included in the sale.
Photos with plastic wrapping removed showing the full keyboard body, back panel, and any visible damage.
response.reason: The item is clearly identifiable as a generic electronic keyboard by type, but brand/model is unreadable and core functional claims (sound, working condition) are unverifiable from photos alone, so it must be priced at the worst-case unverified/unbranded tier pending proof.
